Okay...because I don't remember what all was pictures and what all was text, I'm going to step back and start again from the point of First Appearances only. It shouldn't actually take that long, though I'm not sure when I'll do it.  So going forward with this next draft I'll follow these rules/assumptions...

1) 12 monthly issues or 1 annual per row

2) Comics with no firm evidence otherwise will start at print year 1 while best guesses and assumptions will be noted for logical positioning (ie Expatriatte probably appeared near or after her mother Citizen Dawn...not for sure, but until more obvious evidence appears its likely)

3) All quotes/cards/appearances of a character will be at or after the noted First Appearance (FA) of the character.

4) Freedom Four Annual and Freedom Five Annual are one continuously numbered comic (confirmed by Christopher).

5) Pictures will not be assumed to match the comic quoted on the card (confirmed by Christopher) and will be ignored.

6) If the card is in a given characters deck I'll assume they are in the comic quoted at the bottom, even if they aren't being quoted on the card.

7) If a card quotes someone other then the person who's deck it is, both will be assumed to be in the listed comic.

If any of these assumptions are wrong (most worried about 6 and 7 now that I know pictures don't always match quotes) I hope someone from >G comments to that affect before I get to far into my next attempt.

posts.name: Christopher
posts.cooked: You are fine assuming 6 and 7.

posts.name: Adam
posts.cooked:
With regards to passage of time, it's generally accepted among fans of major comic companies that about 100 issues is equal to 1 year. Lots of times an issue will jump forward in time 6 months, but there's a specific Tachyon-centric issue of Freedom Five I can think of that takes place over the span of 5 seconds. *makes weighing motion with his hands*

This is keeping in mind, however that no time really passes at all. What's important to a comic publisher is that the characters are recognizable 50 years after they were created and haven't become elderly heroes, so they measure time in such small increments that it's negligible over a long time. The ages posted on the characters' bios are their current age in the Sentinel-verse, but they've never been portrayed as much younger than that, and - barring time travel or alternate universes - they'll never be portrayed as much older.
